4º de Primaria · Inglés · Tema 6

Animals and habitats

Nombre: ______________________   Fecha: ___________

Qué vas a aprender

  • Learn the names of wild animals in English
  • Name five habitats: jungle, desert, ocean, polar regions and grassland
  • Describe animals with body parts and adjectives
  • Say where animals live and what they eat with the present simple
  • Compare animals with bigger, faster, smaller (comparar animales)
  • Explain a simple food chain
  • Talk about endangered animals and how to protect them
  • Describe animal adaptations and nocturnal animals

Para pensar

¿Por qué no vemos osos polares en el desierto ni camellos en el Polo Norte?

Explicación

1. What is a habitat?

A habitat is the natural home of an animal or plant. It gives the animal everything it needs: food, water, shelter (refugio) and a place to have babies.

There are many habitats on Earth: jungles (selvas), deserts (desiertos), oceans (océanos), polar regions (zonas polares), grasslands (sabanas y praderas), forests (bosques), rivers and mountains. En castellano: fíjate en que habitat en inglés se escribe sin tilde y casi igual que en español.

2. The jungle

The jungle (or rainforest) is hot and very wet. It rains almost every day and there are very tall trees. Lots of animals live there: monkeys, parrots, snakes, frogs, tigers and jaguars.

Many jungle animals live in the trees. Monkeys have long arms and tails to climb. Parrots have strong beaks to open nuts. Some frogs are very small and very colourful. Frase modelo: «Monkeys live in the jungle. They eat fruit and leaves».

3. The desert

The desert is very dry. It hardly ever rains. During the day it's very hot, but at night it can be cold. There is a lot of sand or rock, and only a few plants, like cactuses.

Desert animals are special: camels can live many days without drinking. Scorpions, snakes and lizards hide under the sand in the hot hours. The fennec fox has very big ears to lose heat. Frase modelo: «Camels live in the desert. They have humps».

4. The ocean

The ocean is the biggest habitat on Earth. It's salty water. Some animals live near the coast and others in very deep, dark water. Here you can find whales, dolphins, sharks, octopuses, turtles, jellyfish and many fish.

Fish breathe with gills (branquias), but whales and dolphins are mammals: they come up to breathe air. Consejo: el plural de fish es igual: one fish, two fish. Y el de octopus es octopuses.

5. Polar regions and grasslands

The polar regions (the Arctic and the Antarctic) are very cold and covered in ice and snow. Polar bears and arctic foxes live in the Arctic (north). Penguins live in the Antarctic (south). They have thick fur or fat to keep warm.

The grassland (savannah) in Africa has lots of grass and few trees. There are lions, zebras, giraffes, elephants and rhinos. Dato curioso: los osos polares y los pingüinos nunca se encuentran, ¡viven en polos opuestos!

6. Endangered animals

Some animals are endangered (en peligro de extinción). This means there are very few of them, and they can disappear forever. When an animal disappears forever, it is extinct (extinguido), like the dinosaurs or the dodo.

Some endangered animals:

  • The polar bear: the Arctic ice is melting because the Earth is getting warmer.
  • The tiger: people cut down its forests, and some people hunt it.
  • The orangutan: its jungle is disappearing.
  • The sea turtle: plastic in the sea is very dangerous for it. It thinks plastic bags are jellyfish!
  • The Iberian lynx (lince ibérico): it lives in Spain and Portugal. There were very few, but now there are more thanks to protection programmes. Good news!

Why are animals in danger?

  • People destroy their habitats.
  • Pollution (contaminación) and plastic.
  • Climate change (cambio climático).
  • Illegal hunting (caza).

What can we do? We can recycle, use less plastic, save water and energy, and never buy products made from wild animals. We can also visit nature reserves and learn about animals.

7. Describing animals: body parts

To describe animals, we use body parts: fur (pelo), feathers (plumas), scales (escamas), wings (alas), tail (cola), beak (pico), claws (garras), fins (aletas), horns (cuernos), trunk (trompa).

We use the verb have got or has got: «A parrot has got feathers and a beak», «Elephants have got a trunk». Also useful: big, small, long, short, strong, fast, slow, dangerous.

8. Comparing animals

To compare two animals, we use comparatives (comparativos) + than (que):

  • Short adjectives: add -er: big → bigger, small → smaller, fast → faster, tall → taller, long → longer, slow → slower.
    «An elephant is bigger than a lion.» «A cheetah is faster than a horse.»
  • Adjectives ending in consonant + vowel + consonant: double the last letter: big → bigger, fat → fatter, thin → thinner.
  • Adjectives ending in -y: change to -ier: heavy → heavier, funny → funnier.
  • Long adjectives: use more: dangerous → more dangerous, beautiful → more beautiful.
    «A shark is more dangerous than a dolphin.»

Some amazing animal facts to compare:

  • The blue whale is the biggest animal in the world. It is bigger than a dinosaur!
  • The giraffe is taller than any other animal.
  • The cheetah is the fastest land animal.
  • A snail is slower than a tortoise. It moves about one metre in an hour!
  • An ostrich (avestruz) is heavier than any other bird, but it can't fly.

Now you: compare your pet or your favourite animal with another animal. Use two or three different adjectives.

Remember: than (que), not that. «A mouse is smaller than a cat.»

9. Where does it live? What does it eat?

We use the present simple to give facts about animals. Remember the -s with it: «The giraffe lives in the grassland. It eats leaves». With plural: «Giraffes live in the grassland. They eat leaves».

Animals that eat plants are herbivores; animals that eat other animals are carnivores; animals that eat both are omnivores. To ask: «Where does the shark live?» – «It lives in the ocean». «What does it eat?» – «It eats fish».

10. Food chains

A food chain (cadena alimentaria) shows who eats who in a habitat. Every food chain starts with a plant, because plants make their own food with sunlight.

Look at this food chain in a meadow:

grass → grasshopper → frog → snake → eagle

  • The grass is a producer (productor): it makes food from sunlight.
  • The grasshopper eats the grass. It is a herbivore (herbívoro).
  • The frog eats the grasshopper. It is a carnivore (carnívoro).
  • The snake eats the frog.
  • The eagle eats the snake. Nothing eats the eagle: it is the top predator (superdepredador).

The arrows (→) mean «is eaten by» (es comido por).

Here is a food chain in the ocean: algae → small fish → big fish → shark.

Some animals eat plants and meat. They are omnivores (omnívoros): bears, pigs, chickens… and people!

Useful sentences:

  • «Frogs eat insects.»
  • «Eagles hunt snakes.»
  • «A predator hunts other animals. The animal it hunts is the prey (presa).»

If one animal disappears, the whole chain is in danger. That's why every animal is important!

11. Reading: animal riddles

Read and guess! 1. «I live in the jungle. I've got a long tail and I can climb trees very well. I eat bananas. What am I?» 2. «I live in the ocean. I'm very big, but I'm not a fish. I breathe air. What am I?» 3. «I live in the Antarctic. I've got black and white feathers, but I can't fly. I can swim very well. What am I?»

4. «I live in the grassland. I'm the tallest animal in the world. I eat leaves from the trees.» Answers: monkey, whale, penguin, giraffe.

12. Let's practise: my animal fact file

Choose your favourite wild animal and make a fact file (ficha). Draw it and complete: Name: …, Habitat: It lives in…, Food: It eats…, Body: It has got…, Abilities: It can… / It can't…, Fun fact: …

Then present it to the class without saying the name. Your classmates guess the animal. Consejo: revisa que todos los verbos con it lleven la -s: lives, eats. ¡Y con has got, no have got!

13. Animal adaptations

Animals have got special body parts and behaviours to survive in their habitat. These are called adaptations (adaptaciones).

  • The polar bear has got thick white fur and a layer of fat to keep warm. Its white colour helps it to hide in the snow.
  • The camel has got a hump (joroba) with fat. It can live for many days without water. It has got long eyelashes to protect its eyes from the sand.
  • The giraffe has got a very long neck to eat leaves from tall trees.
  • The fish has got gills (branquias) to breathe underwater and fins to swim.
  • The chameleon can change colour to hide. This is called camouflage (camuflaje).
  • The penguin can't fly, but it is a great swimmer. Its wings are like flippers.

Some adaptations are about behaviour (comportamiento):

  • Some birds migrate (migran): they fly to warmer places in winter.
  • Some animals hibernate (hibernan): they sleep all winter. Bears and dormice do this.

Use has got and can to describe adaptations: «A camel has got a hump. It can live without water for many days.»

14. Day and night animals

Most animals are active during the day and sleep at night, like us. They are diurnal (diurnos). But some animals do the opposite: they sleep during the day and wake up at night. They are nocturnal (nocturnos).

Nocturnal animals:

  • The owl has got big eyes to see in the dark and very good ears. It can turn its head almost all the way round!
  • The bat flies at night and catches insects. It uses sounds and echoes to find its way.
  • The hedgehog (erizo) looks for worms and snails at night.
  • The fox often hunts at night.
  • The firefly (luciérnaga) lights up in the dark.
  • Many moths (polillas) fly at night.

Why are some animals nocturnal? At night it is cooler (más fresco), so desert animals stay safe from the heat. It is also darker, so it is easier to hide from predators.

Useful phrases:

  • «Owls sleep during the day and hunt at night.»
  • «Is a bat nocturnal? Yes, it is.»
  • «Is a horse nocturnal? No, it isn't. It's diurnal.»

Can you think of a nocturnal animal that lives near your home?

Animals and their habitats

Ejercicios

  1. Translate: selva, desierto, océano, sabana.

  2. Translate: plumas, escamas, pelo, cola.

  3. Where do camels live?

  4. Complete: «The monkey ___ (live) in the jungle.»

  5. Complete: «A lion ___ got sharp claws.»

  6. Name two animals from the polar regions.

  7. Make a question: where / the dolphin / live

  8. What is a herbivore?

  9. Correct: «Giraffes eats leaves.»

  10. Write a riddle about an animal.

  11. Complete: An elephant is ___ (big) than a mouse.

  12. What does a herbivore eat?

  13. Is an owl nocturnal or diurnal?

  14. What is camouflage?

  15. Name an endangered animal.

  16. Complete: A shark is ___ (dangerous) than a dolphin.

  17. Write the comparative of heavy and thin.

  18. Make a food chain in the ocean.

  19. Why are polar bears in danger?

  20. Describe one adaptation of a camel.

  21. Write five sentences comparing animals.

  22. Make a poster to protect an endangered animal.

  23. Describe a nocturnal animal: body, food and habitat.

  24. Invent an animal with special adaptations and describe it.

Practica

  1. «Habitat» means…

    1. A) a type of food
    2. B) a body part
    3. C) the natural home of an animal

  2. Camels live in the…

    1. A) desert
    2. B) ocean
    3. C) jungle

  3. Penguins live in the…

    1. A) Arctic
    2. B) Antarctic
    3. C) desert

  4. «Plumas» is…

    1. A) scales
    2. B) feathers
    3. C) fur

  5. Fish have got…

    1. A) feathers and a beak
    2. B) fur and claws
    3. C) scales and fins

  6. «The shark ___ in the ocean.»

    1. A) lives
    2. B) live
    3. C) living

  7. An animal that eats plants is a…

    1. A) carnivore
    2. B) omnivore
    3. C) herbivore

  8. «Where ___ the tiger live?»

    1. A) do
    2. B) does
    3. C) is

  9. Which animal lives in the grassland?

    1. A) zebra
    2. B) octopus
    3. C) polar bear

  10. The plural of «fish» is…

    1. A) fish
    2. B) fishs
    3. C) fishes

  11. A cheetah is ___ than a horse.

    1. A) more fast
    2. B) faster
    3. C) fastest

  12. Every food chain starts with…

    1. A) an eagle
    2. B) a shark
    3. C) a plant

  13. Endangered means…

    1. A) peligroso
    2. B) en peligro de extinción
    3. C) dormido

  14. A camel has got a ___ with fat.

    1. A) hump
    2. B) neck
    3. C) fin

  15. Nocturnal animals sleep…

    1. A) at night
    2. B) all winter
    3. C) during the day

Explícalo con tus palabras

Incluye: Qué es un hábitat y qué da a los animales; Cómo son la selva, el desierto, el océano y las zonas polares; Cómo se describe un animal con has got; Cómo se dice dónde vive y qué come un animal.
